title: Project: Entanglement Swapping
summary: Entangle two qubits that never interacted by measuring their partners in the Bell basis.
objectives: Entangle two qubits that share no gate by measuring their partners in the Bell basis
Choose corrections on qubit 3 that give the same final state for every measurement result
Compare the entanglement of qubits 0 and 3 before and after the protocol
mission: Qubits 0 and 3 start in separate Bell pairs, (0, 1) and (2, 3), and no gate may act on both. Entangle them anyway: measure qubits 1 and 2 in the Bell basis and apply classically controlled corrections to qubit 3, so that qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ for every measurement result. Record c_before and c_after, the concurrence of qubits 0 and 3 right after creating the pairs and at the end of the circuit.
hints: Start from lesson 1.6: what does Alice's Bell measurement look like, and which two qubits are measured here? Build the two pairs first.

Pairs: qc.h(0), qc.cx(0, 1) and qc.h(2), qc.cx(2, 3). Bell measurement of qubits 1 and 2: qc.cx(1, 2), qc.h(1), then qc.measure(1, 0) and qc.measure(2, 1). Then correct qubit 3 as Bob does: X when the bit of qubit 2 is 1, Z when the bit of qubit 1 is 1.

Each correction goes in a with qc.if_test((qc.clbits[k], 1)): block. For the records, c_before = float(concurrence(partial_trace(final_state(qc), [1, 2]))) right after the pairs, and the same expression again at the end for c_after.

prediction.question: After the Bell measurement on qubits 1 and 2, and even if you know both results, you look at qubit 0 alone. What do you see when you measure it?
options: A fair coin, in any basis: qubit 0 is half of a Bell pair with qubit 3
A definite state that depends on the two results you know
|0⟩ every time, since no gate touched qubit 0 after its pair was made
prediction.explanation: Whatever the results are, qubits 0 and 3 end in a Bell state, and half of a Bell pair is maximally mixed. Qubit 0 is entangled with qubit 3 now, so alone it is a fair coin; the correlation shows up only when the outcomes of 0 and 3 are compared. No gate touched qubit 0, yet its situation changed, because the measurement acted on the state of the whole system.

messages.ok: Qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ in all {total} sampled runs (with {outcomes} different measurement results), with concurrence {before} before and {after} after.
messages.wrong_size: The circuit needs four qubits and two classical bits: qc = QuantumCircuit(4, 2).
messages.forbidden_pair: A gate acts on qubits 0 and 3 together. The point of the protocol is that the two ends never interact, so use gates on (0, 1), (2, 3) and (1, 2) only, and single-qubit corrections.
messages.measured_end: Qubit {qubit} is measured. Only the middle qubits 1 and 2 should be measured, because measuring an end qubit destroys the state you are trying to build.
messages.no_measurement: There is no measurement yet. Qubits 1 and 2 must be measured in the Bell basis (after qc.cx(1, 2) and qc.h(1)), with the results stored in classical bits.
messages.branch_wrong: In none of the {total} sampled runs do qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ (worst fidelity {fidelity}). The problem is probably before the corrections, in the pairs or in the Bell measurement.
messages.branch_partial: Qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ in only {good} of {total} runs (worst fidelity {fidelity}). The pairs and the measurement look fine, so one correction is missing or tied to the wrong bit: X follows the bit of qubit 2, Z the bit of qubit 1.
messages.no_record: The concurrences are not recorded. Store them in c_before and c_after.
messages.before_wrong: c_before = {value}. Right after creating the pairs, qubits 0 and 3 have no correlation, so the value should be 0. Compute it before the measurement.
messages.after_wrong: c_after = {value}. At the end qubits 0 and 3 are in |Φ⁺⟩, so the value should be 1. Compute it after the corrections.
